races.title: State House, District 73
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jonathan Almond
cands.bio: Republican who represented North Carolina House District 73 (Cabarrus County) from January 2025 and lost re-election in November 2026. Controller for a management group operating 11 franchise restaurants since 2016. Holds UNC Charlotte degrees in accounting and finance.

endorsements.text: Listed on the 2026 'Pull mRNA Shots Off the Market' voter guide from the Sway voting group (Mary Talley Bowden, MD), per Ballotpedia.

In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he listed these endorsers himself: Sheriff Van Shaw, Senate Majority Leader Paul Newton, Rep. Kristin Baker, Skip Stam, Larry Pittman, the NC Police Benevolent Association, NC Values Coalition, Grass Roots North Carolina and Students for Life Action. These are self-reported.

cands.gaps: Almond did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. His descriptions of his legislative record come from his own campaign website, and the page was cut off partway through, so his remaining issue positions could not be read. We found no independent reporting on his legislative actions. He says he backed a data-center ratepayer bill (SB 730) requiring data centers to pay for their own power and infrastructure. We found no stated position for or against data centers or new development, so none is recorded. We found nothing on his stance on foreign or institutional land buyers, no documented controversies, and no foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Charlotte, and his campaign biography says he spent his first 18 years in rural Union County and has lived in North Carolina his whole life.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served one term in the North Carolina House (2025-2026). Has worked as controller for a management group operating 11 franchise restaurants since 2016, and holds accounting and finance degrees.
qual.why: He has held legislative office for a term, and his career in accounting and financial management is relevant to the state budget. He has only one term of legislative experience, so the score sits at the low end of the high band.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site says he voted Yea on HB 1089, a constitutional cap on local property tax increases. It also says he served on the House Select Committee on Property Tax Reduction and Reform and describes himself as committed to lowering property taxes. This is his own account; it is not a verified record.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site says he voted Yea on SB 153, which it describes as improving safety, compliance and cooperation with immigration authorities. This is his own account; it is not a verified record.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he voted Yea on HB 307 (Iryna's Law, ending cashless bail for violent offenses) and on the 2026 budget with pay increases for state law enforcement. This is his own account; it is not a verified record.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he will fight against any attempts to infringe on constitutional gun rights. It calls him a Second Amendment Republican.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he voted Yea on the veto override of HB 87 (Educational Choice for Children Act) and on a budget funding 8% teacher raises. This is his own account; it is not a verified record.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site lists $75,000 for Gate Pregnancy Resource Center among the budget items he says he helped secure for Cabarrus County. It does not state a position on abortion restrictions.

prio.label: Matches 6 of 6 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 6 only promised

cands.name: Thomas J. Monks
cands.bio: Democrat from Concord, Cabarrus County. Former Director of Marketing and Partnerships at Anna Lotan PRO USA, with a career in marketing, education and partnership development. Holds a communication degree (public relations) from Florida Gulf Coast University. Won the District 73 House seat in 2026, defeating incumbent Jonathan Almond. No prior elected office is documented.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party (Ballotpedia also lists several Sway voting-group recommendations).

cands.gaps: We found no record of Monks holding elected office, so there is no legislative record to report. We found no stated positions on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. His campaign site says only that he wants affordable housing, support for small businesses and teachers "paid what they deserve," and a high-quality public education. That is too general to match to specific policies. His birth year and exact age when he moved to North Carolina are not given. His work history comes only from his own campaign biography, and we found no independent reporting confirming it. We found no controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign biography says he was born in Florida and raised in North Carolina, moved to Indian Trail in 2007, graduated from Sun Valley High School, and returned in 2015 to buy a home in Concord.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.why: A management-level private-sector career fits the middle band. No prior legislative service or policy or budget work is documented, and the work history comes only from his own campaign site.
